w: A shipping magnate's private hoard turned public treasure house. Sir William Burrell and wife Constance amassed the collection filling these galleries; the museum opened in 1983, reopened in 2022 after refurbishment, and in 2023 won Art Fund Museum of the Year -- the only non-national museum to take that prize twice.
s: A shipping magnate's hoard, twice Museum of the Year
_facts: Houses the art collection of Sir William Burrell and Constance, Lady Burrell
Museum opened in 1983 and reopened on 29 March 2022 after major refurbishment
Won the Art Fund Museum of the Year award in July 2023
The only non-national museum to be outright winner of that prize twice

w: Home turf of the West of Scotland Cricket Club -- and the unlikely birthplace of international football. In 1872 this Partick cricket ground hosted the very first international match, Scotland against England, long before either side had a proper stadium. A quiet pitch, a genuine world first.
s: A cricket ground that hosted football's first international
_facts: Cricket ground in the Partick area of Glasgow, home to West of Scotland Cricket Club
Previously also used for association football
Hosted the first-ever international football match in 1872, Scotland versus England
